issues.failure_explanation: The displayed formula interpolates the raw values $p_j^n$ and $q_j^n$, which contain the factor $\e^{\iu\kappa\xi/\eps}$. A piecewise linear interpolant of such carrier-modulated data has $O(h)$ error when $\kappa h/\eps$ is not small. The prose describes a different, envelope-based implementation, but that is not what the formal reconstruction formula specifies.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\mathcal{I}$ on the envelopes $a_j^{\pm,n}$ and reconstruct via \eqref{eq:pq}--\eqref{eq:upq}, or explicitly use a carrier-aware interpolant, and include the resulting overlap interpolation error in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm}.
issues.overall_effect: The $O(h^2)$ reconstruction guarantee in Theorem~\ref{thm} is unsupported during wave-packet overlap.
issues.title: Overlap reconstruction interpolates carrier-modulated values
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and preserves the advertised second-order accuracy, but the algorithm as formally written does not deliver the reconstruction contract used by the error theorem.

The theorem nevertheless states an unconditional uniform bound at all $x_i$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that the computational interval contains the wave packets and that the neglected truncation error is within the stated tolerance, or explicitly restrict the theorem to the untruncated infinite-grid scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-dimensional error guarantee in Theorem~\ref{thm}, and the analogous polarized statement, is broader than what the analysis establishes.
issues.title: Error theorem ignores finite-interval truncation
issues.why_classification: A local scope hypothesis or explicit exclusion of truncation error repairs the statement without changing the proved estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: For $|\beta|<1$, condition \eqref{eq:stability} permits $\alpha=\vartheta\tau/\eps^2\to0$. At $\theta h=\beta$, $\gamma_\theta\to0$ and $\wt\gamma_\theta\to1$, so the two eigenvalues coalesce and the eigenvector matrix $V(\theta)$ becomes ill-conditioned on the order of $1/|\alpha|$. Thus no $\mu<1$ independent of $\tau,h$ is available, the asserted uniform norm equivalence is not established, and in the limit the recurrence has a Jordan block.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict the stability lemma to $\tau/\eps^2$ bounded away from zero and treat the classical regime separately, or construct a uniform stability norm and error argument that remains valid as $\alpha\to0$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma~\ref{lem:stability} loses its uniform constant, and the uniform error bounds in Theorems~\ref{th:MFE}, \ref{thm}, and \ref{thm:polarized}, as well as the Crank--Nicolson analogue in Lemma~\ref{lem:stability-cn}, are unsupported.
issues.title: Uniform norm equivalence in linear stability fails as tau tends to zero
issues.why_classification: The advertised uniform-in-$\tau,h$ stability statement cannot be repaired locally; it requires excluding the classical regime or a new uniform stability argument.
